explain.es: Para hablar de una situación que empezó en el pasado y continúa ahora, el inglés usa el present perfect + for / since. Aquí está la gran trampa: el español usa el presente («Vivo aquí desde hace tres años»), pero el inglés necesita el present perfect: I've lived here for three years. Piensa en una línea que sale del pasado y llega hasta hoy.
explain.en: For a situation that started in the past and continues now, English uses the present perfect + for / since, not the present simple.

explain.title: 1 · FOR + periodo
explain.es: For va con un periodo: una cantidad de tiempo que puedes contar (diez minutos, dos días, tres años) o expresiones como for ages (desde hace siglos), for a long time, for a while. En español equivale a «desde hace», «llevar + tiempo» o «hace … que».
explain.en: for + a period of time you can count: for ten minutes, for three years, for ages.
formula: have / has + participio + *for* + two hours / a week / ages

examples.en: I've lived in Seville for three years.
examples.es: Vivo en Sevilla desde hace tres años.

examples.en: She's worked from home for six months.

explain.title: 2 · SINCE + punto de inicio
explain.es: Since va con el momento en que empezó la situación: una hora (since 9 a.m.), un día (since Monday), una fecha (since 2020), un evento (since Christmas) o una frase en past simple (since I was a child, since we met). En español: «desde» o «desde que».
explain.en: since + the moment the situation started: since Monday, since 2020, since I was a child.
formula: have / has + participio + *since* + Monday / 2020 / I was ten

examples.en: They've known each other since they were kids.
examples.es: Se conocen desde que eran niños.

explain.title: 3 · Preguntas: HOW LONG…?
explain.es: Para preguntar por la duración usamos How long + have / has + sujeto + participio…? = «¿Cuánto tiempo hace que…?», «¿Desde cuándo…?». Se responde con for o since (o all my life, «toda la vida»). ¡No traduzcas «¿Desde cuándo…?» como Since when are you…?!
explain.en: How long + have / has + subject + participle? Answer with for or since.

examples.en: How long have you had your car? — For two years.
examples.es: ¿Cuánto tiempo hace que tienes el coche? — Dos años.

examples.en: How long has she been your boss? — Since May.
examples.es: ¿Desde cuándo es tu jefa? — Desde mayo.

examples.en: How long have they been married? — For thirty years.

explain.title: 4 · ¿Por qué no el presente?
explain.es: I live here solo dice dónde vives ahora. Si añades una duración (for / since) unes pasado y presente: eso es trabajo del present perfect. También en negativa: «Hace meses que no lo veo» = I haven't seen him for months.
explain.en: Duration up to now → present perfect, never the present simple. Negative: I haven't seen him for months.

examples.en: I've known him for years. (not: I know him for years)
I haven't seen Laura since the summer.
examples.es: No veo a Laura desde el verano.

examples.en: We haven't had a holiday for two years.
examples.es: Hace dos años que no tenemos vacaciones.

explain.title: FOR, SINCE o AGO
explain.es: Las tres hablan de tiempo, pero no son intercambiables. for mide la duración, since marca el inicio y ago dice cuánto tiempo hace que pasó algo terminado: va con past simple y detrás del periodo.
explain.en: for = duration, since = starting point, ago = how long before now (past simple).

explain.title: ¿Sigue o terminó?
explain.es: for también puede ir con el past simple, pero el significado cambia. Present perfect = la situación continúa. Past simple = la situación ya terminó.
explain.en: Present perfect + for = it continues. Past simple + for = it's finished.

explain.note: for = cuánto dura (lo puedes contar). since = cuándo empezó (lo puedes señalar en el calendario).
explain.note_en: for = how long (you can count it). since = when it started (you can point to it).

items.why: Situación que sigue + since → present perfect.
items.why_en: Duration up to now → present perfect.

items.bad: We've been friends since ten years.
She's had this job for June.
How long do you know Marta?
I have lived here three years ago.
items.good: I moved here three years ago. / I've lived here for three years.
items.why: ago va con past simple; for con present perfect.
items.why_en: ago + past simple; for + present perfect.

items.bad: I'm working here for six months.
items.good: I've worked here for six months.
items.why: «Llevo seis meses…» no es presente continuo.

items.bad: Since when are you a vegetarian?
I don't see him since June.

items.es: ¿La situación sigue ahora? → present perfect (have / has + participio).
¿Dices desde cuándo (2020, el lunes, que era niño)? → since.
¿Ya terminó, o dices cuándo pasó? → past simple: I lived there for two years. I moved two years ago.

lines.en: So, Daniel, how long have you lived in Dublin?
lines.es: Bueno, Daniel, ¿cuánto tiempo llevas viviendo en Dublín?

lines.en: For two years. I moved here two years ago, after university.
lines.es: Dos años. Me mudé aquí hace dos años, después de la universidad.

lines.en: And how long have you worked at the café?
lines.es: ¿Y cuánto tiempo llevas trabajando en la cafetería?

lines.en: Since March. Before that, I worked in a hotel for a year.
lines.es: Desde marzo. Antes trabajé un año en un hotel.

lines.en: Your English is excellent. How long have you studied it?
lines.es: Tu inglés es excelente. ¿Desde cuándo lo estudias?

lines.en: Thanks! I've studied English since I was eight, so for about fifteen years.
lines.es: ¡Gracias! Estudio inglés desde los ocho años, o sea, desde hace unos quince años.

lines.en: And how long have you been interested in marketing?
lines.es: ¿Y desde cuándo te interesa el marketing?

lines.en: Oh, for ages! Since I opened my first social media account, really.
lines.es: ¡Uf, desde hace siglos! Desde que abrí mi primera cuenta en redes, la verdad.

explain.title: Truco del calendario
explain.es: Imagina un calendario 📅. SINCE: puedes señalar con el dedo el día en que empezó (2020, el lunes, Navidad). FOR: tienes que contar los días, meses o años que han pasado. ¿Lo cuentas? → for. ¿Lo señalas? → since.
explain.en: Can you point to it on a calendar? → since. Do you have to count it? → for.

items.q: We use «for» with a period of time (two days, a year).
We use «since» with a period of time.
«I live here since 2020» is correct English.
«How long have you known her?» = ¿Desde cuándo la conoces?
«Ago» goes with the past simple: I met her two years ago.
«I've worked here for five years» means I don't work here now.
«I worked there for five years» means I don't work there now.
After «since» we can use a clause: since I was a child.

exercises.text_title: Meet Rosa, the heart of Café Luna ☕
text: Rosa Martín has run Café Luna in Salamanca since 2006. That means she has worked there for twenty years! Before that, she lived in London for three years, where she learnt English and fell in love with good coffee.

Rosa has known most of her customers for years. Some of them have come to the café every morning since it opened. Her favourite customer is Mr Gómez, a retired teacher. He has had the same breakfast — toast and a café con leche — since 2010!

Rosa hasn't had a proper holiday since 2019, but she isn't worried. “I've loved this job since the first day,” she says. “Why would I want a holiday?” Her daughter, Elena, has helped her in the café since last summer, so maybe Rosa will go back to London one day.

items.q: Rosa has run Café Luna for twenty years.
Rosa still lives in London.
items.why: She lived in London for three years, before she opened the café.

items.q: Mr Gómez has had the same breakfast since 2010.
How long has Rosa run Café Luna?
How long did Rosa live in London?
items.a: She lived there for three years.

items.q: When was Rosa's last proper holiday?
items.a: In 2019. She hasn't had a proper holiday since 2019.

items.q: How long has Elena helped in the café?

checklist.es: Uso for + periodo (two years, ages) y since + punto de inicio (2020, Monday).
checklist.en: I use for + a period and since + a starting point.

checklist.es: Uso el present perfect (no el presente) para situaciones que continúan.
checklist.en: I use the present perfect, not the present, for situations that continue.

checklist.es: Pregunto con How long have / has…? y contesto con for o since.
checklist.en: I can ask How long…? and answer with for or since.

checklist.es: Traduzco «desde hace», «llevo…» y «hace … que no…» correctamente.
checklist.en: I can translate desde hace, llevo… and hace … que no…
I know the difference between for, since and ago.

checklist.en: I know past simple + for means it's finished.
